name: Block app access to the camera (this account)
summary: Turn off app access to the camera for your account.
what: Sets the per account app permission for the camera to Deny. This is the value the Windows Settings privacy page writes.
benefit: Apps that ask Windows for access cannot use the camera until you allow it again.
risk: Low. Video calls and photo apps from the Microsoft Store stop seeing the camera until you allow it again. Allow it again in Settings, Privacy and security.
advice: Suggested if no Microsoft Store app needs your camera.
facts: Per account, so other accounts are not affected
Writes the same value the Windows Settings privacy page does
You can allow individual apps again in Settings
Revert restores exactly what was there before

name: Block app access to the camera (all accounts)
summary: Force app access to the camera off for every account.
what: Applies the app privacy policy that forces access to the camera to Deny. Nobody can turn it back on in Settings.
benefit: No Windows app on this PC can use the camera, and nobody can change that from Settings.
risk: Medium. Video calls and photo apps from the Microsoft Store stop seeing the camera until you allow it again. The Settings switch is locked until you revert.
advice: Suggested only for shared or locked down PCs. Most people should use the per account switch instead.
facts: Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Users cannot change it from Settings while it is on
Policies are honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education
Revert removes the policy value
